title: Allow reverse mapping of key to shortcut combo / shortcut combo to key in Keyboard manager

status.label: Feature request, not a confirmed bug
status.detail: The report requests new bidirectional key/shortcut remapping and explicitly labels the scenario as an enhancement.

judgment.rationale: The issue explicitly requests a new reverse/bidirectional mapping capability and includes the Idea-Enhancement label. It describes the limitation of a one-way key-to-shortcut mapping and asks for an option to reverse it; it does not show a failure of an existing documented feature. Keep it out of bug-fix work and route it through feature-request prioritization.
evidence: The title asks to allow reverse mapping of key-to-shortcut and shortcut-to-key.
The body calls for a toggle in the Remap a key dialog and labels the scenario as a feature/enhancement request.
The live issue is open with Issue-Bug and Idea-Enhancement labels, no comments, and no assignees.
Related open issue #49677 concerns a defect in bidirectional Alt/Win key-to-key swaps; its scenario does not cover this requested key/shortcut-combo feature.
judgment.recommended_action: Treat this as a feature request rather than a current bug; no bug-fix proposal or reporter follow-up is warranted from the available evidence.

fix_assessment.rationale: The request is for new bidirectional mapping functionality, not a defect in an existing documented behavior; it belongs in feature prioritization rather than the bug-fix queue.

issue_context.summary: Request for bidirectional mappings so F1-to-Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Z-to-F1 can coexist.
known_information: The author maps F1 to Ctrl+Z and reports that adding the reverse shortcut mapping overrides the first mapping.
The author proposes a reverse-mapping toggle and explicitly describes this as a feature enhancement.
The issue has no comments or assignees.
inferences: The requested behavior may require product-level precedence and loop-prevention rules, but the report does not establish a current bug.
issue_context.analysis: This is an unsupported capability request rather than a confirmed defect: the desired outcome requires adding bidirectional mapping behavior and its conflict semantics. A separate Alt/Win swap bug does not cover this combination.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue body and current labels, comments, and assignees.
Searched current issues for reverse mapping; found #49677, which is an Alt/Win key-to-key defect with a different expected behavior.

next_action.label: Route through feature-request prioritization
next_action.reason: No defect in an existing documented behavior is established; the requested reverse mapping is new functionality.
